analysis: Examined the release-notes change in scripts/provider-release-publication.py (head lines 55-68), its tests, and docs/operations/provider-release.md. release_changelog now runs `git tag --list --format=%(contents)%00%(contents:signature)%00` as a list-argument subprocess with no shell, so tag text stays data and is never executed. The test keeps the $(touch ...) marker check. The output is parsed as bytes: split on NUL into contents and signature, then removesuffix(signature), decode as UTF-8 and strip. If the annotation contains a NUL, the split can produce an unexpected number of fields and raise ValueError. A signed tag cannot carry a NUL, since git rejects NULs in tag messages. This is a fail-closed CI error, not a trust bypass. A non-UTF-8 annotation would raise UnicodeDecodeError at signing time, which is also fail-closed. The changelog only goes into the registration payload (`changelog` field) and the retained release-payload.json. That payload is digest-bound through RELEASE_PAYLOAD_SHA256 and re-validated by checked_payload. The changelog is not part of the validate() identity checks. Its authenticity is covered by the signed-tag check in verify_tag on the prod path. Signature stripping reduces armor leakage into public release notes and does not alter trust decisions. The new tests assert that the payload minus changelog and the bundle/provenance bytes are unchanged, and that tampering with the payload or provenance fails with a digest mismatch. That reinforces the immutability controls. The test helper unsets GIT_DIR and related variables and disables hooks and signing, which is a sound isolation choice. There is no change to the coordinator trust boundary, attestation, App Attest qualification (TB-011, T-054), routing, or provider runtime. The documentation changes are consistent with the code. Remaining open question: the 64 KiB registration body limit applies to the changelog, and the behavior is unchanged. Registration-time enforcement lies outside the supplied evidence.
